claim: Centrosomes act as the main microtubule organizing center (MTOC) in metazoans.
source: Centrosomes act as the main microtubule organizing center (MTOC) in metazoans.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about centrosome function.

claim: Centrosome number is tightly regulated by limiting centriole duplication to a single round per cell cycle.
source: Centrosome number is tightly regulated by limiting centriole duplication to a single round per cell cycle.
evidence: This is established knowledge about centrosome regulation.

claim: PLK4 is the most upstream facilitator of centriole duplication.
source: This control is achieved by multiple mechanisms, including the regulation of the protein kinase PLK4, the most upstream facilitator of centriole duplication.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PLK4's role in centriole duplication.

claim: Altered centrosome numbers in mouse and human cells cause p53-dependent growth arrest.
source: Altered centrosome numbers in mouse and human cells cause p53-dependent growth arrest through poorly defined mechanisms.
evidence: This statement references established findings in the field.

claim: TRIM37 is required for cell cycle arrest in acentrosomal cells.
source: Recent work has shown that the E3 ligase TRIM37 is required for cell cycle arrest in acentrosomal cells.
evidence: This references recent published work.

claim: TRIM37 is a key mediator of growth arrest after partial or full PLK4 inhibition.
source: We found that TRIM37 is a key mediator of growth arrest after partial or full PLK4 inhibition.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screens performed in this study.

claim: PLK4 cellular mobility decreased in a dose-dependent manner after centrinone B treatment.
source: Interestingly, PLK4 cellular mobility decreased in a dose-dependent manner after centrinone B treatment.
evidence: This is based on FRAP experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Growth arrest after PLK4 inhibition correlated better with PLK4 activity than with mitotic length or centrosome number.
source: In contrast to recent work, we found that growth arrest after PLK4 inhibition correlated better with PLK4 activity than with mitotic length or centrosome number.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing multiple experimental results including FRAP, mitotic length measurements, and centrosome counting.

claim: The centrosome consists of two microtubule-based centrioles surrounded by pericentriolar material (PCM).
source: Each centrosome consists of two microtubule-based centrioles surrounded by pericentriolar material (PCM) (Conduit et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Conduit et al., 2015.

claim: Each cell inherits a single centrosome from the previous cell cycle.
source: Each cell inherits a single centrosome from the previous cell cycle and subsequent centriole duplication is restricted to a single round of replication (Gönczy and Hatzopoulos, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Gönczy and Hatzopoulos, 2019.

claim: Centriole duplication initiates at the G1/S transition.
source: Centriole duplication initiates at the G1/S transition and is largely a stepwise pathway dependent on the upstream kinase PLK4 (Gönczy and Hatzopoulos, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Gönczy and Hatzopoulos, 2019.

claim: PLK4 is a low-abundance protein.
source: PLK4 is a low-abundance protein (Fode et al., 1996) that is recruited around the mother centriole (Sonnen et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Fode et al., 1996.

claim: PLK4 is recruited around the mother centriole.
source: PLK4 is a low-abundance protein (Fode et al., 1996) that is recruited around the mother centriole (Sonnen et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Sonnen et al., 2013 and Kim et al., 2013.

claim: PLK4 kinase activity is regulated by interaction with STIL and CEP85.
source: PLK4 kinase activity is regulated by interaction with STIL and CEP85 resulting in the recruitment of SASS6 to form the cartwheel of the nascent daughter centriole followed by the recruitment of centriole elongation factors (Moyer et al., 2015; Ohta et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018; Schmidt et al., 2009; Kohlmaier et al., 2009; Tang et al., 2009; Comartin et al., 2013; Azimzadeh et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: PLK4 functions as a homodimer.
source: PLK4 functions as a homodimer and autophosphorylates itself in trans to generate a phosphodegron sequence that limits its abundance.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PLK4 function.

claim: PLK4 autophosphorylates itself in trans to generate a phosphodegron sequence that limits its abundance.
source: PLK4 functions as a homodimer and autophosphorylates itself in trans to generate a phosphodegron sequence that limits its abundance. This sequence is recognized by SCFβ-TrCP and targets PLK4 for ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis (Rogers et al., 2009; Cunha-Ferreira et al., 2009; Guderian et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Rogers et al., 2009; Cunha-Ferreira et al., 2009; Guderian et al., 2010.

claim: The PLK4 phosphodegron sequence is recognized by SCFβ-TrCP and targets PLK4 for ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis.
source: This sequence is recognized by SCFβ-TrCP and targets PLK4 for ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis (Rogers et al., 2009; Cunha-Ferreira et al., 2009; Guderian et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Rogers et al., 2009; Cunha-Ferreira et al., 2009; Guderian et al., 2010.

claim: Centrosome amplification is a hallmark of tumor cells.
source: Centrosome amplification is a hallmark of tumor cells (Chan, 2011) and may play a role in generating chromosome instability (Ganem et al., 2009; Silkworth et al., 2009) and promoting cell invasiveness (Arnandis et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Chan, 2011.

claim: Centrosome amplification may play a role in generating chromosome instability.
source: Centrosome amplification is a hallmark of tumor cells (Chan, 2011) and may play a role in generating chromosome instability (Ganem et al., 2009; Silkworth et al., 2009) and promoting cell invasiveness (Arnandis et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on cited literature (Ganem et al., 2009; Silkworth et al., 2009).

claim: Centrosome amplification may promote cell invasiveness.
source: Centrosome amplification is a hallmark of tumor cells (Chan, 2011) and may play a role in generating chromosome instability (Ganem et al., 2009; Silkworth et al., 2009) and promoting cell invasiveness (Arnandis et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on cited literature (Arnandis et al., 2018).

claim: Overexpression, inhibition, or deletion of PLK4 results in p53-dependent arrest in cell culture and mouse models.
source: In cell culture and mouse models, overexpression, inhibition, or deletion of PLK4 results in p53-dependent arrest (Holland et al., 2012; Lambrus et al., 2016; Wong et al., 2015; Fong et al., 2016; Marthiens et al., 2013; Coelho et al., 2015; Vitre et al., 2015; Serçin et al., 2016; Hudson et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 screens identified p53, p21(CDKN1A), 53BP1, USP28, and TRIM37 as components of the response to PLK4 perturbation.
source: A series of CRISPR/Cas9 screens identified the p53 pathway members, p53, p21(CDKN1A), 53BP1 and USP28 (Lambrus et al., 2016; Fong et al., 2016; Meitinger et al., 2016), and the E3 ligase TRIM37 as component of this response (Fong et al., 2016; Meitinger et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: A recent screen identified PIDDosome/p53 and ANKRD26 as mediators of supernumerary centrosome-induced arrest.
source: A recent screen for mediators of supernumerary centrosome-induced arrest identified PIDDosome/p53 and placed the distal appendage protein ANKRD26 within this pathway (Evans et al., 2021; Burigotto et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Evans et al., 2021 and Burigotto et al., 2021.

claim: TRIM37 is an E3 ligase associated with multiple cellular functions including gene expression, peroxisome maturation, various signalling pathways, and centriole biology.
source: TRIM37 is an E3 ligase that has been associated with a myriad of cellular functions including gene expression (Bhatnagar et al., 2014), peroxisome maturation (Wang et al., 2017), various signalling pathways (Zhu et al., 2020; Fu et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018), and centriole biology (Balestra et al., 2013; Balestra et al., 2021; Meitinger et al., 2021; Yeow et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: TRIM37 activities have been linked to mono-ubiquitination, poly-ubiquitination, and E3-independent functions.
source: There is no consensus on how TRIM37 mediates these functions since its activities have been linked to mono-ubiquitination (Bhatnagar et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2017), poly-ubiquitination (Zhu et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2020; Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020), and E3-independent functions (Wang et al., 2018) that result in changes in protein activity (Bhatnagar et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2018), localization (Meitinger et al., 2016; Balestra et al., 2021; Meitinger et al., 2021), and abundance (Wang et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2020; Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: In the absence of TRIM37, centriole proteins accumulate to form aberrant assemblies called condensates or 'Cenpas'.
source: In the absence of TRIM37, a collection of centriole proteins such as CNTROB, PLK4, CETN1/2, CP110 accumulate to form aberrant assemblies referred to as condensates or 'Cenpas' (centriolar protein assemblies) (Balestra et al., 2021; Meitinger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Balestra et al., 2021 and Meitinger et al., 2021.

claim: Cenpas are dependent on the presence of CNTROB.
source: These structures are dependent on the presence of CNTROB, but it is unclear why TRIM37 might suppress their formation in normal cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge with an acknowledgment of uncertainty.

claim: TRIM37 is part of the 17q23 amplicon present in approximately 18% of breast cancer tumors.
source: TRIM37 is part of the 17q23 amplicon present in approximately 18% of breast cancer tumors (Kallioniemi et al., 1994) and overexpression of TRIM37 in these lines renders them sensitive to the PLK4 inhibitor centrinone (Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Kallioniemi et al., 1994.

claim: Overexpression of TRIM37 in breast cancer cell lines renders them sensitive to the PLK4 inhibitor centrinone.
source: TRIM37 is part of the 17q23 amplicon present in approximately 18% of breast cancer tumors (Kallioniemi et al., 1994) and overexpression of TRIM37 in these lines renders them sensitive to the PLK4 inhibitor centrinone (Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yeow et al., 2020 and Meitinger et al., 2020.

claim: TRIM37 interacts with PLK4 and CEP192.
source: TRIM37 interacts with PLK4 and CEP192 (Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Meitinger et al., 2020.

claim: TRIM37 can promote ubiquitination of PLK4, but this is distinct from SCFβ−TRCP modification and does not result in changes to PLK4 abundance.
source: Although TRIM37 can promote ubiquitination of PLK4, it is distinct from SCFβ−TRCP modification since it does not result in changes to PLK4 abundance (Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Meitinger et al., 2020.

claim: Transiently overexpressed TRIM37 leads to CEP192 ubiquitination and its subsequent degradation.
source: In contrast, transiently overexpressed TRIM37 leads to CEP192 ubiquitination and its subsequent degradation (Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yeow et al., 2020 and Meitinger et al., 2020.

claim: Treatment with 200 nM centrinone B resulted in cells containing supernumerary centrosomes in approximately 50% of cells.
source: As expected, 500 nM centrinone B resulted in cells containing either a single or no centrosome, but cells treated with 200 nM failed to lose centrosomes and instead accumulated supernumerary centrosomes in approximately 50% of cells (Figure 1C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 1C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D.

claim: Treatment with 500 nM centrinone B resulted in cells containing either a single or no centrosome.
source: As expected, 500 nM centrinone B resulted in cells containing either a single or no centrosome, but cells treated with 200 nM failed to lose centrosomes and instead accumulated supernumerary centrosomes in approximately 50% of cells (Figure 1C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 1C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D.

claim: Treatment with 200 or 500 nM centrinone B results in p53-dependent G1 arrest.
source: Together, these data indicate that centrosomes can be amplified or lost using 200 or 500 nM centrinone B, respectively, and that both phenotypes result in p53-dependent G1 arrest.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Extra centrosomal structures induced by 200 nM centrinone B contained CEP135, CEP120, CETN2, glutamylated tubulin, and could accumulate PCNT and CEP192.
source: Staining for a panel of centriole and centrosome markers revealed that these extra structures contained CEP135, CEP120, CETN2, glutamylated tubulin, and could accumulate PCNT and CEP192 indicating that treatment with 200 nM centrinone B can induce amplification of bona fide centrosomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The Nutlin-3a screen identified core p53 pathway genes TP53, CDKN1A, TP53BP1, and USP28.
source: The Nutlin-3a dataset contained core p53 pathway genes TP53 and CDKN1A and genes coding for p53 regulators TP53BP1 and USP28, consistent with their role in promoting p53 transcriptional activity (Cuella-Martin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: Disruption of BAG6 and EP300 increased fitness in Nutlin-3a treatment.
source: The disruption of both BAG6 and EP300 increased fitness in Nutlin-3a.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: EP300 is an acetyltransferase that binds to and affects the acetylation of p53.
source: EP300 is an acetyltransferase that binds to and affects the acetylation of p53 while BAG6 modulates this acetylation event by EP300 (Sebti et al., 2014; Liu et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Sebti et al., 2014 and Liu et al., 1999.

claim: BAG6 modulates the acetylation of p53 by EP300.
source: EP300 is an acetyltransferase that binds to and affects the acetylation of p53 while BAG6 modulates this acetylation event by EP300 (Sebti et al., 2014; Liu et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Sebti et al., 2014 and Liu et al., 1999.

claim: Inactivation of AHR and ARNT promoted growth when p53 is activated in RPE-1 cells, but not A375.
source: Likewise, inactivation of AHR and ARNT, which form a transcriptional complex activated by exogenous ligands, promoted growth when p53 is activated in RPE-1 cells, but not A375.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: ARNT was previously identified as a FRET interactor with p53.
source: ARNT was previously identified as a FRET interactor with p53 (Li et al., 2017) and interacts with EP300 (Tohkin et al., 2000; Tong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Li et al., 2017.

claim: ARNT interacts with EP300.
source: ARNT was previously identified as a FRET interactor with p53 (Li et al., 2017) and interacts with EP300 (Tohkin et al., 2000; Tong et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Tohkin et al., 2000 and Tong et al., 2016.

claim: Deletion of TSC1/2 caused decreased fitness after p53 activation.
source: Deletion of TSC1/2 that integrates p53 signalling with the mTOR pathway (Armstrong et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2007) caused decreased fitness after p53 activation.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: TSC1/2 integrates p53 signalling with the mTOR pathway.
source: Deletion of TSC1/2 that integrates p53 signalling with the mTOR pathway (Armstrong et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2007) caused decreased fitness after p53 activation.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Armstrong et al., 2017 and Lee et al., 2007.

claim: The 200 nM centrinone B screens identified a core set of 23 genes that suppressed growth arrest in both RPE-1 and A375 cell lines.
source: The 200 nM centrinone B screens (i.e., condition that produces supernumerary centrosomes) revealed a core set of 23 genes that suppressed the growth arrest in both cell lines (Supplementary file 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: The 200 nM centrinone B screens identified the ANKRD26/CASP2/PIDD1/CRADD (PIDDosome) complex.
source: Notably, we identified the ANKRD26/CASP2/PIDD1/CRADD (PIDDosome) complex recently implicated in the response to supernumerary centrosomes (Evans et al., 2021; Burigotto et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: The 200 nM centrinone B screens identified p53 pathway genes (TP53, CDKN1A, TP53BP1, and USP28), centriole duplication factors (CEP85, CENPJ, STIL, USP9X), centriolar satellite proteins (C2CD3, CEP350, KIAA0753, PIBF1), and TRIM37.
source: This set also included p53 pathway genes (TP53, CDKN1A, TP53BP1, and USP28), centriole duplication factors (CEP85, CENPJ, STIL, USP9X), centriolar satellite proteins (C2CD3, CEP350, KIAA0753, PIBF1), and TRIM37.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: The A375 200 nM centrinone B screen identified additional centriole components CP110, CEP97, CEP135, SASS6, CEP76, and PLK4.
source: The A375 screen identified additional centriole components namely CP110, CEP97, CEP135, SASS6, CEP76, and PLK4.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: Twenty-two hits from the 200 nM centrinone B screens overlapped with high-confidence hits from a PLK4 overexpression screen.
source: Twenty-two of the hits from both cell lines combined also overlapped with the high-confidence hits from a similar screen that induced centrosome amplification by overexpressing PLK4 (Evans et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing screen data with published data from Evans et al., 2021.

claim: A total of 37 suppressors were identified probing the response to centriole depletion (500 nM centrinone B), with five scoring in both cell lines (TP53, CDKN1A, TP53BP1, USP28, and TRIM37).
source: We identified a total of 37 suppressors probing the response to centriole depletion (500 nM centrinone B), with five scoring in both cell lines (TP53, CDKN1A, TP53BP1, USP28, and TRIM37).
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: Four of the five common hits from 500 nM centrinone B screens (TP53, TP53BP1, USP28, CDKN1A) were identified by all screens performed to date.
source: Four of the five common hits (TP53, TP53BP1, USP28, CDKN1A) correspond to core p53 pathway components and were the only genes identified by all screens performed to date (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing screen data with published screens.

claim: CHD8 and FBXO42 scored in the 200 and 500 nM centrinone B screens, respectively, but also appeared in Nutlin-3a hits.
source: CHD8 and FBXO42 were previously identified in the response to centrosome loss (Fong et al., 2016) and also scored in our 200 and 500 nM centrinone B screens, respectively; however they also appeared in our Nutlin-3a hits suggesting that these genes might not be specific to centrosome biology.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: FBXO42 and CHD8 are known to negatively regulate p53 activity.
source: Indeed, both FBXO42 and CHD8 are known to negatively regulate p53 activity (Sun et al., 2009; Nishiyama et al., 2009; Lü, 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Sun et al., 2009; Nishiyama et al., 2009; Lü, 2022.

claim: TRIM37 was the only gene outside the p53 pathway that scored in both RPE-1 and A375 cells in both centrinone B concentrations.
source: Two of the previous centriole loss screens also identified TRIM37 (Lambrus et al., 2016; Meitinger et al., 2016) which was unique among all the other hits since it was the only gene outside the p53 pathway that scored in both RPE-1 and A375 cells in both centrinone B concentrations.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: Loss of TRIM37 did not greatly affect centriole amplification or loss after centrinone B treatment.
source: However, centriole amplification or loss after centrinone B treatment was not greatly affected (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A small number of TRIM37-disrupted cells harbored extra centrioles in untreated cells.
source: As previously observed (Balestra et al., 2013), we noted a small number of TRIM37-disrupted cells harbored extra centrioles in untreated cells.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation consistent with published data from Balestra et al., 2013.

claim: p53 and p21 failed to accumulate in TRIM37-/- cells after treatment with 200 or 500 nM centrinone B.
source: After treatment of cells with centrinone B, p53 and p21 failed to accumulate in TRIM37-/- cells at 200 or 500 nM centrinone B (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A small amount of cleaved MDM2 was observed in untreated TRIM37-/- cells with no additional increase after 200 nM centrinone B.
source: We also noted a small amount of cleaved MDM2 (Fava et al., 2017) in untreated TRIM37-/- cells with no additional increase after 200 nM centrinone B.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The MDM2 cleavage product was lost after treatment with 500 nM centrinone B in TRIM37-/- cells.
source: This cleavage product was lost after treatment with 500 nM centrinone B.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: TRIM37 is required for MDM2 cleavage in response to centrinone B treatment.
source: Thus, we find that TRIM37 does not affect gain or loss of centrosomes after centrinone B treatment but is required for the induction of both p53 and p21 in response to these treatments as previously observed (Meitinger et al., 2016), and is required for MDM2 cleavage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: TRIM37 was associated with the centrosome in most cells.
source: Immunofluorescence staining of endogenous TRIM37 indicated that the protein was associated with the centrosome in most cells although it did not strictly co-localize with either γ-tubulin or CEP120 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3C.

claim: TRIM37 localization was detected in all cell cycle stages.
source: To determine if TRIM37 localization was cell cycle-dependent, we co-stained TRIM37 with PCNA and CEP120 (Figure 3D) and detected TRIM37 in all cell cycle stages we could discern.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3D.

claim: TRIM37 localized to both mother and daughter centrioles in most cells.
source: TRIM37 localized to both mother and daughter centrioles in most cells and localized exclusively to the mother or daughter in only a small percentage of cells.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: In cells with two centrosomes, TRIM37 appeared to favor one centrosome over the other.
source: Interestingly, in cells with two centrosomes, TRIM37 appeared to favor one centrosome over the other (Figure 3E, arrowhead) and we observed a minor preference for exclusive association with mother or daughter centrioles in G1 cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3E and G.

claim: FB-TRIM37 formed partial ring structures preferentially surrounding one of the γ-tubulin foci.
source: FB-TRIM37 formed partial ring structures preferentially surrounding one of the γ-tubulin foci.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from 3D-SIM imaging shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The FB-TRIM37 signal was discontinuous with a dot-like distribution around the ring.
source: Moreover, the FB-TRIM37 signal was discontinuous with a dot-like distribution around the ring.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from 3D-SIM imaging shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Both TRIM37 E3 ligase mutants (C18R and ΔRING) localized to the centrosome, albeit at slightly lower levels than the WT protein.
source: Further, we quantified the centrosomal localization of these proteins and found that both E3 mutants localized to the centrosome, albeit at slightly lower levels than the WT protein (Figure 3I and J).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3I and J.

claim: Expression of FB-TRIM37 fully restored the growth arrest triggered by centrinone B.
source: Expression of FB-TRIM37 fully restored the growth arrest triggered by centrinone B as did the expression of either C18R or ΔRING (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Expression of TRIM37 C18R or ΔRING fully restored the growth arrest triggered by centrinone B.
source: Expression of FB-TRIM37 fully restored the growth arrest triggered by centrinone B as did the expression of either C18R or ΔRING (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4A.

claim: TRIM37 promotes growth arrest in response to centrinone B in an E3-independent manner.
source: These data suggest that TRIM37 promotes growth arrest in response to centrinone B in an E3-independent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Robust cell arrest of WT cells was observed after treatment with 125 nM centrinone B or greater.
source: Robust cell arrest of WT cells was observed after treatment with 125 nM centrinone B or greater.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Cells lacking TRIM37 arrested after treatment with very low doses of centrinone B (50–125 nM) but only partially after higher concentrations (≥150 nM).
source: Interestingly, cells lacking TRIM37 arrested after treatment with very low doses of centrinone B (50–125 nM) but only partially after higher concentrations (≥150 nM).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was a dose-dependent increase in centrosome number up to 167 or 200 nM centrinone B after which cells harbored one or no centrosomes.
source: There was a dose-dependent increase in centrosome number up to 167 or 200 nM after which cells harbored one or no centrosomes (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Abnormal centrosome number did not correlate with robust growth arrest in WT cells.
source: Surprisingly, abnormal centrosome number did not correlate with robust growth arrest in WT cells; cell growth was almost completely inhibited at 125 nM centrinone B although we observed minor centrosome abnormalities at this concentration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing experimental data in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: PLK4 mobility decreased with increasing centrinone B concentrations that mirrored growth arrest activity.
source: We expressed a PLK4 reporter construct (GFP-PLK kin + L1) and monitored PLK4 mobility using FRAP after treatment with centrinone B (Figure 4D; Yamamoto and Kitagawa, 2019). PLK4 mobility decreased with increasing centrinone B concentrations that mirrored growth arrest activity.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Phase I response to PLK4 inhibition is TRIM37-independent and occurs at centrinone B concentrations where cells display minor centrosome number aberration (≤125 nM).
source: Phase I is TRIM37-independent and occurs at centrinone B concentrations where cells display minor centrosome number aberration (≤125 nM); a TRIM37-dependent phase II occurs at ≥150 nM centrinone B and can be further separated based on centrosome number; phase IIa cells harbor overduplicated centrosomes (150–200 nM) while phase IIb cells have lost one or both centrosomes (500 nM) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on experimental data.

claim: Phase IIa response to PLK4 inhibition is TRIM37-dependent and occurs at 150–200 nM centrinone B where cells harbor overduplicated centrosomes.
source: Phase I is TRIM37-independent and occurs at centrinone B concentrations where cells display minor centrosome number aberration (≤125 nM); a TRIM37-dependent phase II occurs at ≥150 nM centrinone B and can be further separated based on centrosome number; phase IIa cells harbor overduplicated centrosomes (150–200 nM) while phase IIb cells have lost one or both centrosomes (500 nM) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on experimental data.

claim: Phase IIb response to PLK4 inhibition is TRIM37-dependent and occurs at 500 nM centrinone B where cells have lost one or both centrosomes.
source: Phase I is TRIM37-independent and occurs at centrinone B concentrations where cells display minor centrosome number aberration (≤125 nM); a TRIM37-dependent phase II occurs at ≥150 nM centrinone B and can be further separated based on centrosome number; phase IIa cells harbor overduplicated centrosomes (150–200 nM) while phase IIb cells have lost one or both centrosomes (500 nM) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on experimental data.

claim: Expression of either WT or C18R TRIM37 resulted in growth arrest in the presence of centrinone B.
source: Expression of either WT or C18R TRIM37 resulted in growth arrest although the growth arrest phenotype caused by TRIM37 C18R expression was weaker than that of WT cells.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The growth arrest phenotype caused by TRIM37 C18R expression was weaker than that of WT cells.
source: Expression of either WT or C18R TRIM37 resulted in growth arrest although the growth arrest phenotype caused by TRIM37 C18R expression was weaker than that of WT cells.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4F.

claim: TRIM37 can support growth arrest after PLK4 inhibition in the absence of E3 ligase activity.
source: These data suggest that TRIM37 can support growth arrest after PLK4 inhibition in the absence of E3 ligase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: TRIM37 is required for growth arrest in SASS6-/- cells.
source: We recovered cells lacking centrioles indicating that TRIM37 is also required for growth arrest in these conditions since SASS6 is essential in WT cells (Leidel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: TRIM37-/-SASS6-/- cells were completely resistant to any dose of centrinone B.
source: Interestingly, TRIM37-/-SASS6-/- cells were completely resistant to any dose of centrinone B, unlike TRIM37-/- alone (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Inducible expression of TRIM37 C18R partially rescued the growth arrest phenotype caused by SASS6 loss.
source: Similar to centrosome loss induced by PLK4 inhibition, inducible expression of TRIM37 C18R partially rescued the growth arrest phenotype caused by SASS6 loss (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: Disruption of TRIM37 was unable to suppress growth arrest after PLK4 overexpression.
source: Similar to previous studies (Evans et al., 2021), we found that disruption of TRIM37 was unable to suppress growth arrest in these conditions (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4H, consistent with published data from Evans et al., 2021.

claim: TRIM37 is required for growth arrest after moderate or full PLK4 inhibition.
source: Together, these data suggest that TRIM37 is required for growth arrest after moderate or full PLK4 inhibition and this activity is partially independent of TRIM37's E3 ligase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental results.

claim: TRIM37's growth arrest activity is partially independent of its E3 ligase activity.
source: Together, these data suggest that TRIM37 is required for growth arrest after moderate or full PLK4 inhibition and this activity is partially independent of TRIM37's E3 ligase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental results.

claim: WT RPE-1 cells treated with centrinone B did not exhibit a significant increase in mitotic length until concentrations reached 150 nM.
source: WT RPE-1 cells treated with centrinone B did not exhibit a significant increase in mitotic length, compared to untreated cells, until concentrations reached 150 nM.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The mitotic length of TRIM37-/- cells treated with centrinone B was similar to that of WT cells until concentrations of 200 and 500 nM centrinone B.
source: Strikingly, the mitotic length of TRIM37-/- cells treated with centrinone B was similar to that of WT cells until concentrations of 200 and 500 nM centrinone B; at which point the absence of TRIM37 partially suppressed the increase in mitotic length in WT cells (Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5A, consistent with published data from Meitinger et al., 2020.

claim: The absence of TRIM37 partially suppressed the increase in mitotic length in WT cells at 200 and 500 nM centrinone B.
source: Strikingly, the mitotic length of TRIM37-/- cells treated with centrinone B was similar to that of WT cells until concentrations of 200 and 500 nM centrinone B; at which point the absence of TRIM37 partially suppressed the increase in mitotic length in WT cells (Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5A, consistent with published data from Meitinger et al., 2020.

claim: The increase in mitotic length observed after full PLK4 inhibition (500 nM centrinone B) appears to be dependent on TRIM37 E3 activity.
source: Thus, the increase in mitotic length observed after full PLK4 inhibition (500 nM centrinone B) appears to be dependent on TRIM37 E3 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: TRIM37 E3 ligase activity is not strictly required to suppress pseudo-MTOCs after centrosome loss.
source: Thus, TRIM37 E3 ligase activity is not strictly required to suppress pseudo-MTOCs or to promote cell growth after centrosome loss.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: TRIM37 E3 ligase activity is not strictly required to promote cell growth after centrosome loss.
source: Thus, TRIM37 E3 ligase activity is not strictly required to suppress pseudo-MTOCs or to promote cell growth after centrosome loss.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Stable expression of FB-TRIM37 resulted in a significant decrease in CEP192 that was E3-dependent.
source: We observed a significant decrease in CEP192 that was E3-dependent but did not observe significant changes in PCNT or CEP215 (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: After expression of WT TRIM37 for 4 or 8 hr, a 50–75% decrease in total CEP192 protein was detected.
source: After expression of WT TRIM37 for 4 or 8 hr, we detected a 50–75% decrease in total CEP192 protein (Figure 6C, left panels).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The decrease in CEP192 after TRIM37 expression was E3-dependent.
source: In all cases the decrease in CEP192 was E3-dependent.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Acute expression of WT TRIM37, but not C18R, decreased the intensity of CEP192 and PCNT at the centrosome.
source: Quantification revealed that acute expression of WT TRIM37, but not C18R decreased the intensity of CEP192 and PCNT at the centrosome (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Acute expression of WT TRIM37 decreased the intensity of CEP120 at the centrosome.
source: Interestingly the centriole component CEP120 was similarly diminished at the centrosome indicating that this effect is not specific to PCM proteins (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Overexpression of TRIM37 affects the overall abundance of CEP192 and the mitotic accumulation of CEP192, PCNT, and CEP120 in an E3-dependent manner.
source: We find that overexpression of TRIM37 affects the overall abundance of CEP192 and the mitotic accumulation of CEP192, PCNT, and CEP120 in an E3-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: CEP120 was mislocalized in TRIM37-/- cells and co-localized with CNTROB.
source: We initially observed that CEP120 was mislocalized in TRIM37-/- cells and co-localized with CNTROB (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Ectopic CNTROB structures remained after CEP120 depletion using siRNA.
source: Ectopic CNTROB structures remained after CEP120 depletion using siRNA suggesting that CEP120 is assembled downstream of CNTROB. (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: CEP120 is assembled downstream of CNTROB.
source: Ectopic CNTROB structures remained after CEP120 depletion using siRNA suggesting that CEP120 is assembled downstream of CNTROB. (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: CEP120 and CNTROB were detected in ectopic structures in TRIM37-/- cells and CETN2 foci accumulated near them.
source: We found that CEP120 and CNTROB were detected in these structures and CETN2 foci accumulated near them (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6E.

claim: PLK4 was not detected in the CNTROB/CEP120 structure in TRIM37-/- cells.
source: Notably, we did not detect PLK4 in the CNTROB/CEP120 structure.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6E.

claim: PLK4-3xFLAG was not detected at non-centrosomal aggregates after 3 or 6 hr induction in TRIM37-/- cells.
source: PLK4-3xFLAG was not detected at non-centrosomal aggregates after 3 or 6 hr induction using either anti-FLAG or anti-PLK4 antibodies, despite its accumulation at the centrosome (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: CNTROB/CEP120 assemblies were not affected by the loss of PLK4 activity.
source: Additionally, these assemblies were not affected by the loss of PLK4 activity as they were observed in TRIM37-/- cells treated with 500 nM centrinone B for 3 days (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C, D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C, D.

claim: CNTROB/CEP120 structures disappeared in an E3-dependent manner after stable expression of TRIM37 mutants in TRIM37-/- cells.
source: After stable expression of TRIM37 mutants in TRIM37-/- cells these structures disappeared in an E3-dependent manner (Figure 6F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The suppression of CNTROB/CEP120 structure formation requires TRIM37 E3 ligase activity.
source: We find that CEP120 is a downstream component of the CNTROB structures formed in TRIM37-/- cells and that the suppression of their formation requires TRIM37 E3 ligase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The region from amino acids 505–709 of TRIM37 was sufficient to immunoprecipitate PLK4.
source: Further, the region from amino acids 505–709 of TRIM37 was sufficient to immunoprecipitate PLK4.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: A TRIM37 mutant lacking amino acids 505–709 (FB-Δ505–709) failed to pull down PLK4.
source: Conversely, a TRIM37 mutant lacking this region (FB-Δ505–709) failed to pull down PLK4.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: The association between PLK4 and TRIM37 did not appear to be required for centrinone B-induced growth arrest.
source: Surprisingly, the association between PLK4 and TRIM37 did not appear to be required for centrinone B-induced growth arrest.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 1F, G.

claim: Co-expression of Myc-PLK4 and T7-TRIM37 in HEK293T cells resulted in modification of PLK4.
source: The co-expression of Myc-PLK4 and T7-TRIM37 in HEK293T cells resulted in modification of PLK4 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The modification of PLK4 by TRIM37 was partially dependent on TRIM37 E3 activity.
source: The modification was partially dependent on TRIM37 E3 activity, was not observed when TRIM37 505–709 was expressed, and increased in the presence of TRIM37 Δ505–709.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Treatment of cells with MLN4924 resulted in stabilization of PLK4 but the modified forms remained.
source: Treatment of cells with MLN4924 resulted in stabilization of PLK4 but the modified forms remained (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The slower migrating forms of PLK4 were lost after phosphatase treatment indicating that these modifications are primarily due to phosphorylation.
source: The slower migrating forms of PLK4 were lost after phosphatase treatment indicating that these modifications are primarily due to phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The only treatment that substantially reduced PLK4 phosphorylation was PLK4 inhibition.
source: The only treatment that substantially reduced PLK4 phosphorylation was PLK4 inhibition (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7G.

claim: TRIM37 promotes the accumulation of phosphorylated PLK4 in an E3-dependent manner.
source: Together these data suggest that TRIM37 promotes the accumulation of phosphorylated PLK4 in an E3-dependent manner but this phenomenon does not require robust interaction with PLK4 itself.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 7D, F, and G.

claim: TRIM37 promotion of PLK4 phosphorylation does not require robust interaction with PLK4 itself.
source: Together these data suggest that TRIM37 promotes the accumulation of phosphorylated PLK4 in an E3-dependent manner but this phenomenon does not require robust interaction with PLK4 itself.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The phospho-forms of PLK4 stabilized by TRIM37 likely lie outside the phosphodegron region.
source: Since we observed that TRIM37 promotes PLK4 phosphorylation (Figure 7G), we monitored GFP-PLK4 mobility by FRAP in WT, TRIM37-/- cells and after TRIM37 siRNA but did not observe any differences compared to control cells indicating that the phospho-forms of PLK4 stabilized by TRIM37 likely lie outside the phosphodegron region (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1H, I.

claim: Differential PLK4 inhibition resulted in distinct cellular states.
source: Several observations support our hypothesis that differential PLK4 inhibition used for our screens resulted in distinct cellular states.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations.

claim: MDM2 was cleaved using 200 nM, but not 500 nM centrinone B consistent with excess centrosomes in the former condition.
source: Second, MDM2 was cleaved using 200 nM, but not 500 nM centrinone B consistent with excess centrosomes in the former condition.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The genes derived from each screen (200 nM vs 500 nM centrinone B) were distinct.
source: Last, the genes derived from each screen were distinct.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: ANKRD26/PIDDosome was identified only in the presence of excess centrosomes.
source: Specifically, we identified ANKRD26/PIDDosome only in the presence of excess centrosomes and also identified centriole proteins that, when disrupted, could decrease centrosome load, although we did not formally test this.
evidence: This is a finding from the CRISPR screen data analysis.

claim: Partially inhibited PLK4 reduces its auto-phosophorylation required for its degradation, causing PLK4 to accumulate and promote centriole overduplication.
source: Current models suggest that partially inhibited PLK4 reduces its auto-phosophorylation required for its degradation. As a consequence, PLK4 accumulates and promotes centriole overduplication (Holland and Cleveland, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Holland and Cleveland, 2014.

claim: TRIM37 is involved in mediating growth arrest to partial PLK4 inhibition.
source: While TRIM37 is involved in mediating growth arrest to partial PLK4 inhibition, it is not required for arrest after PLK4 overexpression, which also leads to extra centrosomes (Evans et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data in this study and published data from Evans et al., 2021.

claim: TRIM37 is not required for arrest after PLK4 overexpression.
source: While TRIM37 is involved in mediating growth arrest to partial PLK4 inhibition, it is not required for arrest after PLK4 overexpression, which also leads to extra centrosomes (Evans et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data in this study and published data from Evans et al., 2021.

claim: The fundamental difference between centrosome amplification caused by PLK4 overexpression or by partial inhibition may relate to the per molecule activity of PLK4.
source: The fundamental difference between centrosome amplification caused by PLK4 overexpression or by partial inhibition may relate to the per molecule activity of PLK4, perhaps pointing a role for TRIM37 in regulating PLK4 activity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on experimental observations.

claim: Growth suppression after PLK4 inhibition at any concentration of centrinone B was only partially TRIM37-dependent.
source: Growth suppression after PLK4 inhibition at any concentration of centrinone B was only partially TRIM37-dependent, suggesting that multiple pathways might be activated in these conditions, one dependent on centrosomes and the other dependent on PLK4.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: Multiple pathways might be activated after PLK4 inhibition, one dependent on centrosomes and the other dependent on PLK4.
source: Growth suppression after PLK4 inhibition at any concentration of centrinone B was only partially TRIM37-dependent, suggesting that multiple pathways might be activated in these conditions, one dependent on centrosomes and the other dependent on PLK4.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on experimental observations.

claim: CEP85 and USP9X are genes that might modulate the response to inhibited PLK4.
source: We suggest that the genes unique to our dataset (i.e., low-dose centrinone B treatment) might modulate the response to inhibited PLK4. CEP85 and USP9X are such genes and both encode proteins that affect STIL, a regulator of PLK4 activity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on screen data and known protein functions.

claim: CEP85 is required for robust STIL interaction with PLK4.
source: CEP85 is required for robust STIL interaction with PLK4 while USP9X stabilizes STIL (Liu et al., 2018; Kodani et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Liu et al., 2018.

claim: USP9X stabilizes STIL.
source: CEP85 is required for robust STIL interaction with PLK4 while USP9X stabilizes STIL (Liu et al., 2018; Kodani et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Kodani et al., 2019.

claim: 53BP1 and USP28 were dispensable for growth arrest after PLK4 overexpression.
source: Interestingly, 53BP1 and USP28 were similarly dispensable for growth arrest after PLK4 overexpression (Evans et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Evans et al., 2021.

claim: The MDM2 p60 fragment is known to interact with and stabilize p53.
source: In this case, the MDM2 p60 fragment that is known to interact with and stabilize p53 (Oliver et al., 2011) might be redundant with the function of 53BP1-USP28.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Oliver et al., 2011.

claim: PLK4 activity, by itself, may be a determinant of p53-dependent cell cycle arrest.
source: It is therefore an exciting possibility that PLK4 activity, by itself, may be a determinant of p53-dependent cell cycle arrest.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on experimental observations.

claim: TRIM37 is proposed to mediate the degradation of CEP192 that affects PCM assembly in mitotic cells treated with PLK4 inhibitors.
source: TRIM37 is proposed to mediate the degradation of CEP192 that in turn affects PCM assembly in mitotic cells treated with PLK4 inhibitors (Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020), however, there is no consensus on the exact centrosome or centriole TRIM37 targets.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yeow et al., 2020 and Meitinger et al., 2020.

claim: There is no consensus on the exact centrosome or centriole TRIM37 targets.
source: TRIM37 is proposed to mediate the degradation of CEP192 that in turn affects PCM assembly in mitotic cells treated with PLK4 inhibitors (Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020), however, there is no consensus on the exact centrosome or centriole TRIM37 targets.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of uncertainty in the field.

claim: The effects of TRIM37 on PCM might be dependent on overexpressed TRIM37 or that the TRIM37-/- cell line acquired a genetic or epigenetic change that suppresses effects on PCM proteins.
source: We did not detect reciprocal changes in protein levels in TRIM37-/- cells (Figure 6A) suggesting that the effects on PCM are dependent on overexpressed TRIM37 or that the TRIM37-/- cell line acquired a genetic or epigenetic change that suppresses effects on PCM proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on experimental observations.

claim: Current models of TRIM37 growth arrest function after PLK4 inhibition have primarily focused on mitotic length.
source: Current models of TRIM37 growth arrest function after PLK4 inhibition have primarily focused on mitotic length (Lambrus et al., 2016; Meitinger et al., 2016; Yeow et al., 2020; Meitinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from multiple sources.

claim: After complete PLK4 inhibition, mitotic length and growth arrest were not well correlated and not long enough to activate a 'mitotic timer'.
source: After complete PLK4 inhibition, cells containing one or no centrosome arrested, but in these studies, mitotic length and growth arrest were not well correlated and not long enough to activate a 'mitotic timer' (Wong et al., 2015; Lambrus et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Wong et al., 2015 and Lambrus et al., 2015.

claim: Small increases in mitotic length over multiple cell cycles might be equivalent to a single mitosis with a larger delay.
source: This led to the speculation that small increases in mitotic length over multiple cell cycles might be equivalent to a single mitosis with a larger delay (Lambrus et al., 2016; Meitinger et al., 2016) but this possibility has not yet been tested.
evidence: This is a speculative statement cited from Lambrus et al., 2016 and Meitinger et al., 2016.

claim: Treatment with 50 nM and 125 nM centrinone B led to ~25% and 90% decreases in cell proliferation, respectively, without causing concomitant increases in mitotic length.
source: First, in WT RPE-1 cells, we observed that treatment with 50 nM and 125 nM centrinone B led to ~25% and 90% decreases in cell proliferation, respectively (Figure 4B) without causing concomitant increases in mitotic length (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4B and Figure 5A.

claim: A significant difference in growth between WT and TRIM37-/- cells was observed at 125 nM centrinone B or greater but significant differences in mitotic length were not detected until treatment with 200 nM centrinone B.
source: Second, when comparing WT and TRIM37-/- cells, we observed a significant difference in growth between these cell lines at 125 nM centrinone B or greater but did not detect significant differences in mitotic length until a treatment with 200 nM centrinone B.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4B and Figure 5A.

claim: Induced expression of TRIM37 C18R caused a partial reduction in cell proliferation without any apparent effect on mitotic length.
source: Third, induced expression of TRIM37 C18R caused a partial reduction in cell proliferation without any apparent effect on mitotic length (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: PLK4 overexpression in mice or flies results in increased mitotic indices indicative of lengthened mitoses.
source: We also note that PLK4 overexpression in mice or flies results in increased mitotic indices (Marthiens et al., 2013; Basto et al., 2008) indicative of lengthened mitoses, yet TRIM37 is not required for growth arrest under similar conditions in cultured cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Marthiens et al., 2013 and Basto et al., 2008.

claim: TRIM37 is not required for growth arrest after PLK4 overexpression in cultured cells.
source: We also note that PLK4 overexpression in mice or flies results in increased mitotic indices (Marthiens et al., 2013; Basto et al., 2008) indicative of lengthened mitoses, yet TRIM37 is not required for growth arrest under similar conditions in cultured cells.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Mitotic length after treatment with 200 and 500 nM centrinone B is clearly affected by TRIM37.
source: Mitotic length after treatment with 200 and 500 nM centrinone B is clearly affected by TRIM37 but our data does not suggest that this directly influences growth arrest.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Mitotic length does not directly influence growth arrest after PLK4 inhibition.
source: Mitotic length after treatment with 200 and 500 nM centrinone B is clearly affected by TRIM37 but our data does not suggest that this directly influences growth arrest.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: Low amounts of ubiquitinated PLK4 were detected only after co-expression with the TRIM37Δ505–709 mutant.
source: Although others have observed TRIM37-dependent ubiquitination of PLK4 (Meitinger et al., 2020), we detected low amounts of ubiquitinated PLK4 only after co-expression with the TRIM37Δ505–709 mutant (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7E.

claim: TRIM37 primarily promoted PLK4 phosphorylation in a manner that was dependent on PLK4 activity itself.
source: In contrast, we found that TRIM37 primarily promoted PLK4 phosphorylation in a manner that was dependent on PLK4 activity itself (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7F and G.

claim: A level of PLK4 inhibition that does not affect centriole number initiates p53 arrest independent of TRIM37.
source: A level of PLK4 inhibition that does not affect centriole number initiates p53 arrest independent of TRIM37, but cell arrest after further PLK4 inhibition becomes dependent on TRIM37.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Cell arrest after further PLK4 inhibition becomes dependent on TRIM37.
source: A level of PLK4 inhibition that does not affect centriole number initiates p53 arrest independent of TRIM37, but cell arrest after further PLK4 inhibition becomes dependent on TRIM37.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: TRIM37 promotes phosphorylation of PLK4.
source: TRIM37 itself promotes phosphorylation of PLK4 and can affect the abundance and/or localization of CEP192, PCNT, and CEP120, but the effect of these functions is not clear.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7.

claim: TRIM37 can affect the abundance and/or localization of CEP192, PCNT, and CEP120.
source: TRIM37 itself promotes phosphorylation of PLK4 and can affect the abundance and/or localization of CEP192, PCNT, and CEP120, but the effect of these functions is not clear.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6.

claim: SASS6 was required for growth arrest at all centrinone B concentrations.
source: SASS6 was required for growth arrest at all centrinone B concentrations, (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) suggesting that centrioles themselves may play a role to integrate the growth arrest signal.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Centrioles themselves may play a role to integrate the growth arrest signal.
source: SASS6 was required for growth arrest at all centrinone B concentrations, (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) suggesting that centrioles themselves may play a role to integrate the growth arrest signal.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on experimental observations.
